questions.q: Why is "the Azure SDK for Python" actually many separate packages instead of one?
options: It's a single monolithic package with no internal structure at all
It's split by service area — azure-mgmt-compute, azure-mgmt-storage, azure-mgmt-network, and more, each following the same client pattern
Each package only works in a different programming language
Microsoft has never consolidated its Python tooling into a single package
questions.explain: The Azure SDK is deliberately split into a family of azure-mgmt-* packages, one per service area, all following the same client-object shape.

questions.q: What is the shared pattern every azure-mgmt-* package follows?
options: Build a *Client object from a credential and subscription ID, then call methods on it
Each package uses a completely different, unrelated syntax
Call a REST endpoint directly with no client object at all
Import the package but never instantiate anything
questions.explain: Whether it's ComputeManagementClient or StorageManagementClient, the construction pattern — credential plus subscription_id — stays identical.

questions.q: What's the real difference between boto3.client() and boto3.resource()?
options: There is no real difference between the two
client() is the low-level interface mirroring the AWS API call-for-call; resource() is a higher-level, more Pythonic interface for a subset of services
resource() is deprecated and should never be used
client() only works for Azure, and resource() only works for AWS
questions.explain: client() names methods exactly as AWS names its API operations, while resource() offers a more object-oriented layer for services like S3 that support it.

options: A plain string containing the VM's name only
Nothing — it's only used to delete virtual machines
Real VM objects with usable attributes like name and location, not raw JSON to parse by hand
An error unless run from inside the Azure portal
questions.explain: The Azure SDK converts the raw API response into proper Python objects with real attributes like .name and .location.

questions.q: What three steps do both the Azure SDK and Boto3 reduce to, once you're past the import line?
options: Build a client (or resource) with credentials, then call a method and get structured data back
There are no shared steps between the two SDKs
Install a new package for every individual API call
Write raw HTTP requests by hand for every single operation
questions.explain: Despite different package structures, both SDKs follow the same underlying shape: import, build a client with credentials, call a method.
